2026 SEMA Show • Ford Frostwarden, a Bronco SUV With Over 1,200 HP, the R125 and F-250 Also in Tow
2026 SEMA Show: Ford Frostwarden, a Bronco SUV With Over 1,200 HP, the R125 and F-250 Also in Tow
8 photos
Photo: Ford
There are so many cool things happening at the 2026 SEMA Show , like Billie the Pontiac GTO from Ringbrothers (just to give you an example off the top of our minds), that Ford felt compelled to break the norm. Then it sliced it into pieces, burned it, spread the ashes, and blew them away with a wind turbine rather than a simple leaf blower. Yeah, that pretty much sums it up.
Anyway, before we even consider talking about Frostwarden, let’s just say that the Blue Oval also had other interesting things to showcase. One of them was a 1966 Ford Mustang Fastback “built from heritage” and named Ford Racing R125. That’s because, quite obviously, it’s a Mustang Fastback with Ford Racing parts, making it a feisty restomod that celebrates Ford Racing’s 125th Anniversary with a 347-cubic-inch crate engine producing 360 horsepower and 400 lb.-ft. of torque and a Tremec TKX-600 five-speed transmission at its heart.
There are way more things going on with it, but we need to jump a couple of decades to reach Matt Johnson, a mechanical engineer who decided to morph a forgotten 1985 Ford F-250 into a “showstopper.” So, he took the $800 truck and made it look pretty, then dropped the ​​​​Ford Racing 460-cube small block in it with 575 hp and 575 lb-ft of torque. After becoming the water tank discussion subject in Dearborn, Ford reached out to him and convinced the builder to make it a SEMA contender.
Skip a few other decades, and we’re in present time right out in Las Vegas, Nevada, where the “SEMA builds do more than stop you in your tracks.” So, Ford aimed to be outrageous and over the top and make dreams possible, and the result is Frostwarden. The name is quite odd, since the only references outside of the Blue Oval news we could find are about a legendary melee weapon in Dungeon Quest or an ancient geomancer in Minecraft.
Anyway, the Blue Oval version is “the first vehicle to put the new Megazilla 2.0 crate engine swap on full display,” a Ford Bronco paired with a supercharged 7.3-liter V8 that can pack over 1,200 horsepower and over 1,000 lb.-ft. of torque. The SUV is strapped in with “the kind of hardware required to give that power an equally serious platform: 42-inch BFGoodrich tires, custom 18-inch Weld bead-lock wheels, 74Weld portal gear lifts, upgraded Dana driveline hardware, and custom Bilstein dampers.”
The brief was simple: “go big.” So, the Megazilla 2.0 is a “new development program with a stronger block, supercharger-specific camshaft, upgraded pistons, larger fuel injectors, a different belt drive and damper, and a 3.0-liter Gen 6 Whipple supercharger at the center of the package.” Ford says it’s the most powerful crate engine ever created by an automaker “based on race fuel per SAE J607 standard.”
The SUV is also leaning into the direction of a Bronco Arctic search-and-rescue rig, so the “42-inch tires, portal gear lifts, and wide stance give Frostwarden the presence of a serious winter recovery machine,” complete with all the attributes needed to stand out in a tall crowd as the one at the annual SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada. Of course, don’t count on this Bronco hitting the trails in series production form, quite sadly, as Ford expressly says it’s not quite up to snuff with the “federal safety standards.” It’s still cool, though.
